---
title: "Resources"
subtitle: "Everything here is free"
---

## Books (all free PDFs)

| Book | Role |
|------|------|
| [Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong — *Mathematics for Machine Learning*](https://mml-book.github.io/) | The backbone (Modules 1–4); has its own exercises + notebooks |
| [Boyd & Vandenberghe — *Convex Optimization*](https://stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/) | Constrained optimization, duality, LP/QP |
| [MacKay — *Information Theory, Inference and Learning Algorithms*](https://www.inference.org.uk/itprnn/book.pdf) | Information theory as inference — Module 5's soul |
| [Solomon — *Numerical Algorithms*](https://people.csail.mit.edu/jsolomon/share/book/numerical_book.pdf) | Floating point, conditioning, Gauss-Newton |
| [Murphy — *Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction*](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) | Modern reference for MLE/MAP/conjugacy |

## Notes & cheatsheets

| Resource | Use |
|----------|-----|
| [CS229 Linear Algebra Review](https://cs229.stanford.edu/section/cs229-linalg.pdf) | Module 1 handout |
| [CS229 Probability Review](https://cs229.stanford.edu/section/cs229-prob.pdf) | Module 3 handout |
| [Berkeley Math4ML notes (Garrett Thomas)](https://gwthomas.github.io/docs/math4ml.pdf) | 50-page consolidated review of Modules 1–4 |
| [The Matrix Cookbook](https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~hwolkowi/matrixcookbook.pdf) | Identity reference for Module 2 |
| [Parr & Howard — Matrix Calculus for Deep Learning](https://explained.ai/matrix-calculus/) | Jacobian shape conventions |

## Video courses

| Course | Why |
|--------|-----|
| [3Blue1Brown — Essence of Linear Algebra](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/linear-algebra) · [Essence of Calculus](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/calculus) | The visual language this course speaks; assigned pre-watches |
| [Tübingen — Math for Deep Learning (Geiger)](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/fachbereiche/informatik/lehrstuehle/autonomous-vision/lectures/math-for-deep-learning/) | 18 refresher micro-lectures, 3.5 h total — ideal pre-course |
| [MacKay — Information Theory lectures](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLruBu5BI5n4aFpG32iMbdWoRVAA-Vcso6) | 16 lectures; games, puzzles, and the compression ↔ inference unification |
| [MIT 18.065 — Strang, Matrix Methods](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-065-matrix-methods-in-data-analysis-signal-processing-and-machine-learning-spring-2018/) | SVD as the centerpiece of applied linear algebra |
| [Stanford EE364a — Boyd, Convex Optimization](https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee364a/) · [2023 videos](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoROMvodv4rMJqxxviPa4AmDClvcbHi6h) | Recognition-and-modeling approach; homework archives |
| [Solomon — Applied Numerical Algorithms](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQ3UicqQtfNv_Io_NT1b0Nzr9YDqpK3Lb) | The reference for floating point → Gauss-Newton |
| [CMU 10-606/607 — Math Foundations for ML](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~mgormley/courses/606-607-f18/schedule.html) | The closest sibling course; slides public |
| [Karpathy — micrograd](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMj-3S1tku0) · [makemore](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaCmpygFfXo) | Build autodiff and a bigram LM by hand — our A1 and A3 in video form |
| [fast.ai — Computational Linear Algebra](https://github.com/fastai/numerical-linear-algebra) | Top-down, notebook-driven; randomized SVD, robust PCA |
